answers.prompt: On a scale of 0–5, how excited are you to use this path again? Why?
answers.text: Resident tmux and detach are solid; remote entry still asks me to establish the Station tunnel.

answers.prompt: On a scale of 0–5, how easy was the happy path? What still felt heavier than it should?
answers.text: The page states the exact forwarding boundary and never exposes a public listener.

answers.prompt: On a scale of 0–5, how optimal does this feel vs how it should work? What is missing?
answers.text: A future authenticated Station-native attach could remove one transport setup step.
tmux remains the PTY authority, so SSH and mosh expectations stay intact.

answers.prompt: Even if nothing broke, what felt annoying or dull?
answers.text: I still establish remote forwarding outside the browser.

answers.prompt: If you could demand one change next week, what is it?
answers.text: Offer Station-native authenticated forwarding when the transport and identity contracts are ready.

answers.prompt: What should we never do on this path?
answers.text: Never bind the bearer-token control plane publicly.

answers.prompt: Would you recommend this experience to a peer? (yes/mixed/no + why)
answers.text: Yes for local and SSH-forwarded use; the trust boundary is honest.

featureRequests.title: Station-native authenticated session forwarding
featureRequests.problem: Remote users establish the Station tunnel outside the session browser.
featureRequests.desiredOutcome: An authenticated Station transport forwards the loopback control plane without public bind or new credentials.
featureRequests.smallestExperiment: Integrate only after Station transport and user-scoped identity contracts expose a forwarding port.
